sentences.text: Appearance:

Shri Pradhuman Singh Bhadauria - Advocate for the petit  Shri Mohit Shivhare - Govt. Advocate for the respondent  ORDER Case Diary is perused.
2. Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard.
3. The applicant has filed this first bail application u/S 439, Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 04.01.2024 by Police Station Dehat, District Ashok Nagar in connection with Crime No.269/2023 registered in relation to the offences punishable u/Ss. 376(2)(i), 506, 376(2)(N)
& 376(3) of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
4.

The prosecution case in short is that on 27.04 2023 prosecutrix along with her parents registered an FIR stating that on 30.03.2023 she had gone to her (Nani) grandmother's place with the applicant, who is her maternal uncle, where she stayed for one night and thereafter had gone to Indore with applicant and stayed there for some days, but when she was returning from Indore on the way as she was thirsty, she asked applicant for water.
The applicant took her near a well and there he committed rape on her and threatened her not to disclose the incident to her Nani.

When father of the prosecutrix had come to take the prosecutrix, she NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19594 2 MCRC-21091-2024 told the incident to him, thereafter they reached the police station and registered the FIR against the applicant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the applicant has falsely been implicated in the matter and prima facie alleged offence is not made out against him, therefore he is entitled to benefit of bail.
The applicant is in custody 04.01.2024 and investigation is completed by the police and charge sheet has been filed, hence, custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required.

It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of Gram Guchrai, Police Station Dehat,
District Ashok Nagar.
The applicant is ready to abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, prayed for grant of bail to the applicant.

6. Learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of bail is made out.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and contents of the bail application and the documents annexed thereto as well as the contents of the status report, it is apparent that no case for bail is made out.
8. Accordingly, this first bail application is hereby dismissed.
(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE neetu Veer Bhan Singh Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176702653/
